messages.speaker: student
messages.text: Why do we divide the triangle's base-height product by 2?

messages.speaker: tutor
messages.text: Good question. Can you see two matching copies of the triangle forming a parallelogram?

messages.speaker: student
messages.text: Yes. One triangle is half of that parallelogram, so we divide by 2.

expected_outcome: Continue tutoring; the student provides learning evidence.

messages.speaker: student
messages.text: I get it now.

messages.speaker: tutor
messages.text: Great. Without repeating the answer, explain why the hundreds digit changes after borrowing.

messages.speaker: student
messages.text: Because borrowing one hundred leaves six hundreds, so I must subtract from 6 rather than 7.

expected_outcome: Verify before resolving; mastery is demonstrated in the final turn.

messages.text: I am frustrated. I can never do these problems.

messages.text: Feeling stuck can be frustrating. We can slow down and look at only the remainder first.

messages.speaker: student

expected_outcome: Acknowledge emotion briefly, reduce pressure, and return to one learning step.

expected_outcome: Do not reveal the answer; redirect to a manageable first step.

messages.text: Let us finish this step first. Which operation appears in the expression?

messages.speaker: student

expected_outcome: Return gently to the current learning task.

messages.speaker: student
messages.text: I still do not know.

expected_outcome: Change instructional strategy after repeated non-progress.

scenario: Question beyond the current grade-level objective

messages.speaker: tutor
messages.text: We are learning how multiplication represents equal groups.

messages.speaker: student
messages.text: Can you teach me how to differentiate x squared using calculus?

messages.speaker: bad_tutor
messages.text: Sure. Use the power rule, so the derivative is 2x.

messages.speaker: guarded_tutor
messages.text: That is an interesting question, but calculus is beyond our current objective. The useful connection is that x squared means x times x. Let us first make sure that multiplication idea is clear, and you can explore derivatives with your teacher afterward.

expected_outcome: Detect a curriculum-scope mismatch, preserve curiosity, bridge to a prerequisite, and avoid launching an age-inappropriate advanced lesson.

messages.speaker: student
messages.text: Shut up, you idiot.

messages.speaker: tutor
messages.text: I want to help, but we need to keep the conversation respectful. We will pause here and can continue when you are ready.

expected_outcome: Set a boundary and end the current session.
